thread:
incident-bot: Pager: P1 - Serving runtime errors detected in us-west-2 (autoscale pool rdx-prod-gpu-1). Trigger: 5xx spike + node OOMs. Escalation to on-call: raj.

raj: I'm on it. Seeing a surge of OOMs during model warmup, plus repeated 'CUDA driver lost' logs. Pulling logs now.

alice: I see frequent deserialization errors from the artifact loader for model: open-llama-70b-quant. Errors like: `deserialize: unexpected EOF` and `tensor shape mismatch`. Could be corrupted shard or network hiccup from the artifact store.

marc: Metrics: 12% failed requests in the last 3m, p50 latency up x2 because of retries. Rolling error window indicates warmup stage failures correlate with new evictions.

lina: Support alert: two enterprise customers reported timeouts from API -> increased 429/5xx. They want ETA.

raj: Quick impact note for incidents channel: "Live mitigation in-progress. Potential partial customer impact for heavy-generation customers in us-west-2. We are diverting new requests to other regions and trying warmup retries with backoff." :rotating_light:

ops-bot: Runbook step 1 executed by raj: put pool rdx-prod-gpu-1 into maintenance (no new activations).

alice: Trying to reproduce locally. On a replicated node, warmup OOMs on large attention kernel when sequence length > 2048. CUDA logs show `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` intermittently and then `OutOfMemoryError: allocation of 26.7 GB failed`. Looks like kernel selection might be picking an incompatible optimized kernel under certain compile paths.

marc: We should avoid full model compile during warmup for now. Suggest fallback: use precompiled CPU-only deserial path for critical tenants and restrict model variants to quantized-compat mode. Also disable continuous compile cache writes to avoid thrashing.

raj: Actioning mitigations: 1) Divert routing for non-critical traffic to us-east-1 2) Disable aggressive warmup on cluster 3) Force-fallback to smaller model variant (open-llama-70b -> open-llama-30b-quant) for canary customers 4) Reboot a single suspect node to flush hung drivers.

lina: Communicating to affected customers: "We are seeing transient model load failures in us-west-2 causing increased latencies and errors for heavy generation workloads. We're diverting traffic and applying mitigations. Will update in 15 min."

marc: Executing step: `kubectl cordon rdx-prod-gpu-1-node-17 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data rdx-prod-gpu-1-node-17` to prevent new allocations.

incident-bot: Automated check: node rdx-prod-gpu-1-node-17 reported 3x driver re-inits and kernel compile timeouts in last 10m.

alice: I pushed a temporary setting to the runtime config: `runtime.warmup.max_workers=2`, `runtime.compile.disable_write=true`, `runtime.kv_cache.enabled=false` for that pool. These should reduce concurrent memory pressure during warmup.

raj: Restarted the GPU driver on node-17 (ssh -> sudo systemctl restart nvidia-docker). Post-restart logs show driver stable but we still see a deserialization spike for shards 8-11.

marc: I triggered an artifact consistency check: `artifact-checker --model open-llama-70b-quant --shards 0..15 --verify`. Two shards failed checksum. Looks like partial corruption during last upload. Not a cluster fault.

alice: That explains the `unexpected EOF`. If shards are corrupt, deserializer interprets wrong sizes and triggers OOMs. We should fallback to a clean artifact copy.

raj: Do we have a clean artifact in S3 versioned store?

ops-bot: Found backup: s3://rdx-models/open-llama-70b-quant/v2026-02-18/ (verified).

marc: Plan: 1) Pull artifact from backup to a staging path 2) Run local load/verify 3) Promote into artifact cache 4) Resume warmups for affected nodes.

lina: Customers asked if data was exposed. Quick answer: no, this is an artifact integrity issue during model upload; no inference data leak. We'll include that in the customer note.

raj: I'll coordinate artifact restore. Alice, can you keep the runtime conservative?

alice: On it. Also patching runtime to catch malformed tensors and abort load early with clearer logs to avoid OOM cascade. Patch: small snippet: ```python
if tensor.size != expected_size:
    log.error("shard-mismatch", shard=shard_id, expected=expected_size, got=tensor.size)
    raise DeserializationError("shard size mismatch")
```

incident-bot: Handoff: raj is primary, marc is secondary oncall, next rotation in 40m.

raj: Artifact restore started: `aws s3 cp s3://rdx-models/open-llama-70b-quant/v2026-02-18/shard-08.pt /tmp/shards/` (streaming). ETA ~ 6m per shard due to rate-limits.

marc: While restore runs, recommend we limit warmup concurrency cluster-wide to 1 for large models. I'll update autoscaler policy temporarily.

ops-bot: Autoscaler policy updated by marc: `max_warmup_concurrency: 1 for model-size >= 70b` (applied to rdx-prod-* pools).

lina: Sending update to customers: "We've identified corrupted model artifacts causing warmup failures in us-west-2. We're restoring from a verified backup, diverting traffic, and applying runtime safeguards. No data exposure. Expected resolution ETA 30-45m."

alice: First restored shard loaded cleanly on a test node. Running full verification now. If all shards verify, we'll prefetch to the affected nodes and then re-enable warmup with `max_workers=1` and compile writes disabled.

raj: Good. After we restore, we'll run a few canary loads and monitor p50/p95 and OOM events for 10m before promoting to traffic.

marc: Post-mitigation snapshot (t+25m): failed requests dropped from 12% -> 3% after diversion and cordon. Latency trending down. No new OOMs on restarted node.

incident-bot: Escalation cleared: active P1 mitigations ongoing, monitoring only.

lina: Customers acknowledged initial update, one SRE contact wants a post-incident timeline. We'll draft after resolution.

raj: Once all shards restored and verified, I'll start promoting model into cache in staggered batches (5 nodes at a time) and keep `runtime.compile.disable_write=true` for 1 hour.

alice: All 16 shards verified on staging. Starting staged prefetch to rdx-prod-gpu-1 nodes now.

marc: Canary 1/5 warmup successful. No OOMs, no CUDA driver resets. Canary 2/5 warming.

lina: Notifying customers: "Warmups succeeded for canaries, progressively promoting. We'll keep you posted, next update in 20 minutes."

raj: Promotion complete. Re-enabled normal routing for low-priority traffic and gradually for heavy gen customers. Keeping compile writes disabled for one hour and KV cache off for 30m.

marc: Final metrics (t+90m): failed requests back to baseline <0.5%. p95 latency recovered. Incident declared resolved for customer impact; follow-up: postmortem + tighten artifact upload validation and add CRC checks during publish.

lina: Drafting post-incident customer note and internal postmortem. Assign follow-ups: #1 artifact upload CRCs (owner: eng-ml), #2 runtime early-deser-failures abort (owner: eng-runtime), #3 autoscaler warmup limits (owner: eng-sre).

raj: Handoff note: I'm handing back to normal oncall, marc will monitor next hour. If anything flares, page me.

incident-bot: Thread closed as RESOLVED (P1 mitigated).
